title: Koch's postulates as a slogan that LTBI breaks
dek: Isolate, disease, re-isolate. Wikipedia method history. NAAT-positive paucibacillary disease and LTBI are why the slogan is not a lab SOP.
story: Koch's postulates on Wikipedia are a 19th-century causal checklist: found in disease, isolable, sufficient to cause disease, re-isolable. They were a hygiene slogan against miasma, not a PCR protocol.
Mtb breaks a naive reading constantly: LTBI has evidence of infection without current disease; TBM may be NAAT-positive and culture-stingy; humans are not guinea pigs you ethically re-challenge.
Modern causal talk in this studio lives closer to stats potential-outcomes and to WHO case definitions. Keep the postulates as history that still ambushes exam questions.
deep: Asymptomatic infection is the first snap.
Unculturable or extremely fastidious organisms (leprae) snap isolation.
Molecular detections without isolates snap 'pure culture'.
Do not deny TBM because postulates were not fulfilled in the CSF.

visual.caption: The full slogan demands isolate+challenge; the reduced clinical model accepts NAAT/syndrome. The gap is not a failed diagnosis.
